# Rekon CFD

> Rekon is a browser-based aerodynamic analysis tool for RC flying wings. It combines a live 3D source-doublet panel method (CL, CD-induced, Cm, trim, static margin) with an on-demand D3Q19 lattice-Boltzmann flow-field solver (pressure, streamlines, vorticity, a speed contour plane). It runs as a hosted preview at rekoncfd.vercel.app and as a free, standalone, self-updating desktop app (Windows or macOS) that does the actual solving locally and offline.

Rekon is built for people designing RC flying-wing aircraft who want real lift/drag/trim numbers before cutting foam or filament, without needing a full commercial CFD license or a CAD-heavy workflow.

## Key facts

- Free and open source. Source code: https://github.com/chiragvx/rekoncfd
- Two solvers: a source-doublet panel method for fast, interactive CL/CD/Cm as you drag angle of attack, airspeed, or center of gravity; and a D3Q19 lattice-Boltzmann solver for a full 3D flow field (pressure, streamlines, vorticity hotspots, a speed contour plane).
- Also computes trim (bisection search for Cm=0), static margin about a given CG, and full alpha-sweep polars.
- Accepts STL geometry import (with manual axis/unit override when auto-detection guesses wrong) or a built-in NACA 4/5-digit airfoil and wing generator (span, taper, sweep, dihedral, washout).
- Supports a real banked-flight animation: each frame is a genuine re-solve (fresh panel-method factorization plus a full LBM run) on the mesh rotated to that frame's bank angle, not a cosmetic overlay.
- The hosted web page at rekoncfd.vercel.app is a preview shell only -- it has no backend of its own to solve anything against. The actual solvers only run inside the downloaded desktop app, which starts a local server on 127.0.0.1 and serves the same UI fully offline.
- Desktop app ships for Windows (a single unsigned .exe, no installer) and macOS on Apple Silicon (installed via a Terminal one-liner since there's no Apple Developer ID to notarize against yet). Both check GitHub Releases on launch and update themselves in place.

## Pages

- Homepage: https://rekoncfd.vercel.app/ -- product overview, screenshots, FAQ, and the desktop app download for Windows or macOS (at the #download section)
- Tool: https://rekoncfd.vercel.app/tool -- the live 3D solver (needs the downloaded desktop app to actually compute anything)
- Explore Models: https://rekoncfd.vercel.app/explore -- a gallery of ready-to-fly sample planforms
- Airfoil Generator: https://rekoncfd.vercel.app/airfoils -- NACA 4/5-digit section + wing generator
- Source code and issue tracker: https://github.com/chiragvx/rekoncfd
